evidence.text: The model answered for 99% of scans.
2 scan(s) where the model's diameter differs from the label by more than 4.2 mm (3x the reference spread). Worth a manual look.
The model caught 6 of 7 aneurysms (sensitivity 86%, plausible range 49% to 97%; reference 89%). Balanced accuracy 0.92, G-mean 0.92.
Diameter error: on average 0.6 mm (reference 0.7 mm); 95% of scans within 2 mm; bias -0.1 mm.
The model's aorta outline overlaps the expert outline well in most scans (median Dice 0.96, reference 0.98); 2% of scans are below 0.90.

evidence.value: lowest of Dice x 100, % within size tolerance, sensitivity x 100

notes: R2 is unreliable with this few scans and a narrow diameter range; compare errors in mm and the random-vs-patient gap instead.
Subgroups with only 1-2 aneurysms give meaningless sensitivity numbers; they are listed but should not be interpreted.

provenance.source: SlicePoint hackathon POC (notebooks + POC spec), via data-contract-inventory.md
provenance.author: SlicePoint student team; transcribed by slicepoint-schemas
provenance.notes: Reproduces the POC, not a clinical recommendation. Conflicts: (1) min group size is 12-14 in the spec vs n>=15 in the notebook flag_row; the notebook value 15 is used. (2) The spec's Dice UI markers (0.81/0.90) differ from the notebook/monitor Dice thresholds (red 0.85 / yellow 0.90), which are kept in triggers. (3) The spec says population SD; the notebook mixes population and sample SD; slicepoint-core uses population SD (ddof=0) throughout, see core PARITY.md. (4) monitor.py emits the 'Aneurysms the model caught' row with worse='high' when there are fewer than 3 aneurysms (value n/a); the intended direction is low and that is what is stored here. (5) The notebook-specific rules (triggers with snake_case keys and `parameters`) were added for slicepoint-core milestone 1; they are transcribed from test_your_hospital.ipynb and are what the five checks read.
